predictions: The variant will not produce a reproducible TF-dependent allelic effect in the relevant cells. Any disease association, if present, would require another explanation.

chains.title: TFAP2E binding change with a possible nearby regulatory effect
chains.element: A possible nearby regulatory element, including the dELS cCRE 42 bp away; the variant does not overlap the cCRE.

links.claim: TFAP2E is a tentative candidate: its own QBiC-SELEX model predicts stronger in-vitro binding to ref T than alt G. Related TFAP2 factors have the same mapped-model prediction; TFAP2E is favored here because it has an own-model result and the highest reported HCT 116 expression among TFAP2A, TFAP2C, and TFAP2E. Occupancy at the variant is unestablished.
The nearby dELS cCRE is a possible regulatory context, but it is 42 bp from the variant and its reported activity is a maximum across biosamples, not evidence that the variant affects it in HCT 116.
PYDC2 is a tentative candidate target based on proximity to the variant and its inclusion among genes near the cCRE; regulation of PYDC2 by this variant or cCRE has not been shown.
HCT 116 is a plausible context because TFAP2E is expressed there, but expression alone does not establish occupancy or regulatory activity at this site.
A TFAP2E-to-PYDC2 contribution to colorectal cancer remains speculative; the supplied evidence does not establish this path or a direction of expression or disease effect.

predictions: If this chain is correct, a variant-dependent TFAP2E effect should be detectable in relevant cells, with greater binding to ref than alt; any effect on PYDC2 expression remains directionally unspecified.
TFAP2E-specific occupancy or perturbation should be more informative for this chain than EBF4-specific occupancy or perturbation.
falsified_if: A sufficiently sensitive assay in relevant cells finds no TFAP2E occupancy or variant-dependent TFAP2E effect.
Perturbing the variant or its regulatory context produces no TFAP2E-dependent regulatory or target-gene effect.

links.claim: EBF4 is a tentative candidate because its own QBiC-SELEX model predicts substantially stronger in-vitro binding to ref T than alt G. The prediction is not supported by demonstrated occupancy at the variant.
The nearby dELS cCRE is a possible regulatory context, but it is 42 bp from the variant and its reported activity is not specific to HCT 116 or evidence of an effect from this variant.
PYDC2 is a tentative candidate target based on proximity and nearby-gene annotation; regulation by this variant or cCRE has not been demonstrated.
HCT 116 is a possible context because EBF4 is expressed there, but expression does not establish occupancy or regulatory activity at the variant.
An EBF4-to-PYDC2 contribution to colorectal cancer is unsupported by the supplied evidence, which gives no direction for a gene-expression or disease effect.

predictions: If this chain is correct, a variant-dependent EBF4 effect should be detectable in relevant cells, with greater binding to ref than alt; any effect on PYDC2 expression remains directionally unspecified.

Candidates are TFs whose ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks contain the variant and that are expressed (DepMap line ACH-000971), bound here before bound elsewhere, then a strong site before a weak one, then by |z|; then expressed TFs ENCODE never assayed whose best model passes the gate (occupancy unknown). Shown: 0 of 0 occupied (0 with a strong site), 5 of 85 with unknown occupancy. Left out: 16 TFs assayed in the matching biosample and 557 assayed only elsewhere, none with a peak here. The gate (|z| > 4.05, Bonferroni over 997 models) marks a change QBiC-SELEX detects; it says nothing about occupancy. Effect > 0 means the alternate allele binds more strongly. In vitro binding only. Site strength is the better allele's best k-mer over the variant, as a percentile of the best model's k-mers; a strong site reaches the 97.5th.
